verbalization: Zileuton's relationship with Cyp2c9 is mediated through its structural resemblance to Acetylsalicylic Acid, a well-known nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug that inhibits Cyp2c9. The shared structural features between Zileuton and Acetylsalicylic Acid suggest a potential mechanism of action involving enzyme inhibition, as evidenced by the binding of Acetylsalicylic Acid to Cyp2c9. This structural similarity may allow Zileuton to exert a similar effect, potentially inhibiting Cyp2c9 as well. The lowest common ancestors of Zileuton and Acetylsalicylic Acid, both belonging to the class of organic cyclic compounds and enzyme inhibitors, further support this inference. The evidence suggests that Zileuton may act as a competitive inhibitor of Cyp2c9, leveraging its structural resemblance to Acetylsalicylic Acid to modulate enzyme activity.
